about: Russian official, state media and independent channels, kept apart on purpose.
Ministries and state agencies are the Russian state speaking for itself; the independent
and exiled outlets are not a counterweight to them, only a different unverified account,
and several publish under Russian wartime media law. All are graded at the same floor.
Each entry was loaded and parsed from its public preview page on 16 September 2026 and had
posted within the preceding week unless noted. Channels dropped during that check are
recorded in ``docs/TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_COVERAGE.md`` rather than guessed at here.

channels.name: Russian Ministry of Defence
channels.operator: Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation
channels.reason: The Russian military's own daily briefings and claimed results, issued by a belligerent about its own war.

channels.name: Russian Ministry of Defence (English)
channels.operator: Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation
channels.reason: English edition of the Russian MoD briefings, the version aimed at international audiences.

channels.name: Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
channels.operator: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
channels.reason: Russian diplomatic statements, sanctions responses and briefings in Russian.

channels.name: Russian MFA (English)
channels.operator: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation
channels.reason: English-language Russian foreign ministry messaging, the text quoted abroad.

channels.name: EMERCOM of Russia
channels.operator: Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Russian Federation
channels.reason: Russian emergency service reporting on fires, floods and incident response, including strikes inside Russia.

channels.name: Bank of Russia
channels.operator: Central Bank of the Russian Federation
channels.reason: Rate decisions, capital controls and sanctions responses from the institution that issues them.

channels.name: RIA Novosti
channels.operator: Rossiya Segodnya, a Russian state media group
channels.reason: State wire agency; the fastest carrier of Kremlin announcements and their framing.

channels.name: TASS
channels.operator: TASS, the Russian state news agency
channels.reason: The state news agency of record; official statements in full, with state editorial direction.

channels.name: Izvestia
channels.operator: Izvestia, part of the National Media Group
channels.reason: Kremlin-aligned daily; carries defence and security briefings ahead of the official channels.

channels.name: Readovka
channels.operator: Readovka, a pro-Kremlin Russian news outlet
channels.reason: High-volume pro-government outlet used to test and spread official narratives.

channels.name: Meduza
channels.operator: Meduza, an exiled Russian newsroom based in Latvia
channels.reason: Leading independent Russian-language newsroom, designated undesirable in Russia; reports what state media omits.

channels.name: Mediazona
channels.reason: Court, prison and casualty-verification reporting, including its named Russian military deaths count.

channels.name: Agentstvo
channels.operator: Agentstvo, an independent Russian investigative outlet
channels.reason: Investigative reporting on the Russian state and economy, largely from open Russian records.

channels.name: ASTRA
channels.operator: ASTRA, an independent Russian journalists' collective
channels.reason: Incident reporting from inside Russia, including drone strikes and refinery fires the authorities do not confirm.

channels.name: Ostorozhno Novosti
channels.operator: Ostorozhno Novosti, an independent Russian outlet
channels.reason: Fast independent Russian breaking news, including incidents inside Russia.

channels.name: Baza
channels.reason: First Russian source on many domestic incidents; its reported security-services sourcing is a bias as well as an advantage.

channels.name: SHOT
channels.reason: High-tempo Russian incident reporting, including drone attacks inside Russia; frequently first and frequently wrong.

channels.name: RBC
channels.operator: RBC, a Russian business media group
channels.reason: Russian business and economic reporting on sanctions, budget and industry, published under Russian wartime media restrictions.

channels.name: Kommersant
channels.reason: Established Russian business daily; defence-industrial and economic detail, published under Russian wartime media restrictions.
